title: Finite-stage etale Verdier biduality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites. Here $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ denotes the full subcategory of bounded constructible complexes having finite Tor amplitude: there are integers $u\leq v$ such that, for every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules placed in degree zero, $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^LM)=0$ for $i\notin[u,v]$, using the ordinary etale Tor-amplitude definition [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

For every separated finite-type $X/k$, write $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for its structure morphism. The natural map

$$
\delta_K:K\longrightarrow D_XD_XK
\qquad(K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A))
$$

is an isomorphism. Here $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$, $\omega_X=Ra_X^{\times}A$ is the ambient dualizing object, and $\delta_K$ is the transpose of evaluation, as specified in [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. Consequently $D_X$ is an exact contravariant anti-equivalence of $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$.

proof.text: Identify the paper finiteTorConstructibleEtale predicate with the source constructibleFiniteTor predicate. Boundedness is equivalent by the standard t-structure homology criteria; finite-valued constructibility is equivalent to source constructibility. The Tor predicates agree by hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn, widening [a,b] to [min(a,b),b] in the reverse direction. This handles the zero complex without assuming a nonempty amplitude interval.

The positive-level coefficient quotient is finite. Its additive exponent divides l^n: l lies in the maximal ideal of the coefficient integers, so l^n lies in its nth power, the defining quotient ideal. The residue characteristic is p and l differs from p, hence l^n is a unit in the algebraically closed geometric field. This constructs HasInvertibleExponent for the lifted quotient.

Specialize the already proved source theorems isIso_verdierDualDoubleDual_app and constructibleFiniteTor_verdierDual to this finite coefficient ring and the algebraically closed geometric field. Transport their hypotheses and the preservation conclusion through step 1. The source double-dual transformation is the canonical transpose of evaluation; retain the ambient_duality_pairing witness as well.

Apply ObjectProperty.liftDualEquivalence to the specified contravariant Verdier functor, its canonical natural double-dual transformation, preservation, and componentwise invertibility. Its restriction followed by inclusion is definitionally the original functor following opposite inclusion, so Iso.refl supplies the requested natural isomorphism.

For exactness use etaleHomComparison_thickLocus with the identity coefficient homomorphism. Restriction of scalars along the identity is naturally isomorphic to the identity (first on sheaves, then on derived categories). Its scalar-extension left adjoint is therefore an equivalence and is triangulated by the adjunction shift structure. The thick-locus theorem supplies triangulatedness of internal Hom followed by scalar extension. Reflect this property through the scalar-extension equivalence with isTriangulated_iff_comp_right; CommShift.ofComp supplies the compatible shift structure. Apply map_distinguished and spell out its third arrow to obtain the exactness clause. The three constructibility assumptions on a triangle are harmless since this is ambient exactness.

It is not a duplicate of lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality, which has no explicit degree interval. lem-sf-etale-twisted-bidual-transport is true by symmetric-monoidal coherence: under alpha, evaluation becomes ev' tensor 1_J, J cancels, and theta cancels between the two Hom variables.
